text:
ciaran: FYI noticed a ~14% drop in prefix cache hit-rate after yesterday's kernel roll and tokenizer bump. Latency tail climbed on a subset of endpoints.
perf-bot: alert: prefix-cache-hitrate drop detected for cohort 'web-chat' (-13.9%) window=1h. p95 latency +120ms.
bryan: repro steps? is this only for requests with tool calls / function args?
ciaran: looks correlated with requests that include tool metadata and long system prompts. Quick grep: most misses have slightly reordered tool arg JSON or trailing spaces in system prompt.
elaine: we did also pin tokenizer -> v2.4 in the rollout (for a tokenization bugfix). Could be tokenization changes shifting key fingerprints.
marta: if tool arg ordering is nondeterministic on the caller side, cache key collisions/misses are expected. We should canonicalize caller-visible fields before fingerprinting.
sam: +1. Minimal canonicalizer rules: trim whitespace, collapse internal whitespace, stable sort arrays of objects by name/id for 'tools' and 'functions', remove ephemeral request IDs from keys.
ciaran: can we do that in the runtime path before cache keying? hooking into prekey pipeline?
bryan: yes, there's a prehash hook used for KV cache sampling. We can add a fast-normalize there. Keep it cheap.
sam: pseudo: 
```
def normalize_key(payload):
    payload['system'] = payload['system'].strip()
    payload['prompt'] = re.sub(r'\\s+', ' ', payload['prompt'])
    if 'tools' in payload:
        payload['tools'] = sorted(payload['tools'], key=lambda t: t.get('name',''))
    return json.dumps(payload, separators=(',', ':'), sort_keys=True)
```
ciaran: that looks fine but watch out: changing canonicalization is itself a key schema change. We need migration/rollout plan to avoid cold-start spike.
elaine: also tokenizer pin: if v2.4 tokenizes quotes differently, two normalization passes (pre-tokenizer normalization and post-tokenizer fingerprinting) might diverge. We should pin both tokenizer and fingerprint version in the key metadata.
marta: propose key format: "v=2|tok=v2.4|canon=v1|sha=..." so we can rotate canon/tok separately and still route to compatible caches.
bryan: good call. That gives us safe fallbacks when we change the canonicalizer.
perf-bot: metric: noncanonical-hit-ratio=0.11 for affected cohort; avg payload size +3% (system prompt trimming needed).
ciaran: quick experiment idea: normalizer-only backend (no kernel rollback) on 5% traffic. Keep logs for both pre/post-normalizer key and measure hit reduction.
sam: add a metric to log keys hashed by version metadata so we can see dual-key hits. e.g., emit: {orig_key, canon_key, tok_version}. Keep payload sampling small.
elaine: operational note: deploy-bot shows the last deploy changed kernel flags for continuous-batching. Could the kernel reorder vectors affecting small differences?
deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-14T02:12Z by @infra-team, tags: kernel-batching-v3, tokenizer-v2.4-pin.
ciaran: tl;dr: likely 2 contributors: tokenizer tokenization surface change + nondeterministic tool arg order. Plan: 1) add cheap canonicalizer in prehash hook behind feature flag; 2) include key metadata with tok/canon versions; 3) A/B 5-10% traffic, monitor hit-rate and p95; 4) if good, ramp to 50% then 100% with migration path; 5) keep kernel rollback on standby if tail persists.
bryan: who owns the initial patch? I can PR the prehash hook + flag.
marta: I'll draft the canonicalization tests and add a fuzz test that randomly orders keys to assert stable key output.
sam: I'll add telemetry for dual-key emissions and a dashboard for 'canon rollout' cohort.
ciaran: assign: bryan=prehash PR, marta=tests, sam=metrics/dashboard, elaine=rollback playbook + tokenizer compatibility notes. I'll run the 5% experiment after we have the flag and tests.
bryan: PR target EOD, small change. Will include feature-flag gating and unit tests.
marta: quick note: avoid deep JSON normalization for nested opaque blobs (attachments) — only normalize fields we control.
ciaran: agreed. Keep canonicalizer white-listed fields: system, prompt, tools/functions, tool args that are part of call spec.
perf-bot: will emit a new metric: canonicalizer.applied=true/false and cache_key_version.
elaine: thanks, team. If the 5% shows >8% hit recovery we roll. If kernel rollback required, call-out infra on pager. :thumbsup:
ciaran: cool. I'll post follow-up once PRs land and we start measurement.
elaine: FYI I'll also pin a note in the runbook about key schema versioning to avoid accidental incompatible rolls next time.
ciaran: end of thread.
